name: Artemis IV
fact: Planned as the first crewed lunar landing since Apollo 17 in 1972 — a gap of more than 55 years, and the first ever near the south pole. The target is the water ice in permanently shadowed craters, which may one day supply drinking water, oxygen and rocket propellant. Artemis IV took this role in 2026, when NASA turned Artemis III into an Earth-orbit test; it is planned for early 2028.
capability: Human polar surface operations and in-situ resource utilisation rehearsal — the direct precursor to crewed Mars missions, which will depend on polar water ice for both consumables and propellant.
